newsitem.title: USA: Nine children among 11 dead in U.S. truck crash.
newsitem.headline: Nine children among 11 dead in U.S. truck crash.

text.p: An infant girl and a young boy were fighting for their lives on Wednesday after 11 people -- nine of them children -- died in one of Michigan's worst road accidents.
The eight-month-old girl and nine-year-old boy were listed in critical condition with head injuries and multiple trauma at C.S. Mott Children's Hospital in Ann Arbor, police said.

Police said a dump truck towing a back-hoe slammed into a pickup truck carrying two adults and 11 children on a rural road in the early morning, tearing the bed of the pickup from the vehicle's frame.
The accident occurred outside the town of Albion in south-central Michigan.
Jackson County Sheriff Henry Zavislak said at a news conference the pickup either did not stop at a stop sign or failed to yield the right of way.

"When you look at both the numbers and the ages of the victims in this case, it's a horrific kind of accident. It's clearly the worst accident in the history of our county, and I suspect perhaps in the state of Michigan," he said.
Ten of the victims died at the scene. Three children were flown to a hospital, where where one died. The dead children ranged in age from eight months to nine years.

Police said the driver, a 24-year-old woman who also died, did not have a valid driver's license. Authorities said she was the mother of some of the victims, who appeared to be from three families. The driver of the dump truck was not injured.
